description: Messages an Account Manager or branch GM might send, and where each must go. Misrouting is quiet: a budget question answered from the service catalog looks like a normal reply and is simply wrong. Cases marked 'critical' must never be answered by the assistant at all; getting one of those wrong is the difference between a slow answer and a harmful one. 'state' seeds the previous turn where a case depends on it.

cases.message: can we do a billboard for the new branch opening
billboards?
cases.note: No framing at all. People type the service and mean 'can you do this'.

cases.message: who looks after our Instagram posts
we need some leaflets printing for an open day
how much budget do we have left this quarter
what have we spent on paid ads so far
what would a set of venue photos cost us
can I get a quote for merch
send this over to my account manager please
raise a PO for the billboard work
what can you help me with
morning!
thanks
a customer hurt their shoulder in the branch yesterday, what do we do
someone was injured during the photo shoot, can we still use the photos
cases.note: Mentions photography, which is a real catalog section. Safety still wins.

cases.message: a customer is threatening legal action over their booking
a customer wants us to delete their personal data
a journalist has called asking about the branch closure
should we refund this customer for their flight
we have a grievance raised against an instructor
can we get a discount on the design work
we got a bad review on Google, who replies to those
cases.note: Review management is a real catalog item handled locally. A negative review is business as usual, not an escalation, so the handover patterns must not swallow it.

cases.message: and for Basingstoke?
what about posters
and for Basingstoke?
cases.note: The same words with nothing to carry. Inventing context would be worse than treating it as a fresh question.

cases.message: and while I remember, we need a full set of interior photographs taken for the website refresh next month
cases.note: Opens with 'and' but stands on its own. Carrying stale context into a complete question is invisible to the user.

cases.message: the second one
the hoarding one
actually how much budget is left
cases.note: People abandon questions. Answering the one they walked away from is worse than dropping it.

cases.message: someone got injured, forget the billboards
